column1: pluralistic§The pluralistic model works only where four separate authorities agree on who settles a dispute.§这套**多元的**模式只在四个独立当局对由谁裁决争议达成一致时才行得通。§plural（复数，同 plural 复数的）
poetic§The report has a poetic clarity that no committee document has any business possessing.§这份报告有一种**诗意的**清晰，是任何委员会文件都不该具备的。§
poignant§The most poignant detail is the shopping list on the back of the last letter he ever sent.§最**令人心酸的**细节是他寄出的最后一封信背面的购物清单。§pung（刺，同 puncture 刺穿）→ 扎心
polarization§The polarization is recent: on the same question in 1994, the two sides differed by four points.§这种**两极分化**是近来的事——1994 年就同一问题，两派只差四个百分点。§pol（极，同 pole 极点）
polarize§The proposal polarized a town that had agreed on almost everything for the previous forty years.§这项提案让一个此前四十年几乎事事一致的小镇**分裂对立**起来。§
polemic§The polemic against the reforms is better written than the reforms and considerably less accurate.§这篇反对改革的**檄文**写得比改革本身好，也远不如它准确。§
politicize§Politicizing the appointment cost the institution nine years of independence it has not recovered.§把这项任命**政治化**让这家机构失去了九年独立性，至今没能恢复。§
polymath§The polymath published in four fields and is now remembered, unfairly, for the least important of them.§这位**博学者**在四个领域发表著作，如今却不公平地只因其中最不重要的一项而被记住。§poly（多）+ math（学习，同 mathematics 数学）
pomp§The pomp of the ceremony cost four times what the scholarship it announced was worth.§典礼的**排场**花费是它所宣布的那项奖学金的四倍。§
pompous§The pompous introduction promised a landmark study and was followed by a competent, modest, and rather short paper.§这段**浮夸的**引言许诺一项里程碑式研究，接下来的却是一篇称职、朴素而且相当短的论文。§
poorly§The scheme was poorly designed and well funded, and it ran for nine years before anyone evaluated it.§这个方案设计得**很差**而资金充足，运行九年才有人评估。§
popularity§The popularity of the route is now its main problem: four hundred walkers a day on a path built for forty.§这条路线的**受欢迎**如今成了它的主要问题——为四十人修的小径每天走四百人。§popul（人民，同 people 人民）
portent§The drought of 1974 was read as a portent, and the four that followed were read as weather.§1974 年的旱情被当作**凶兆**，而随后的四次被当作天气。§por（向前）+ tent ← tend（伸展，同 tension 张力）
portray§The film portrays him as a reluctant hero, and his own letters show a man who volunteered four times.§这部电影把他**刻画**成不情愿的英雄，而他自己的信显示他四次主动请缨。§por（向前）+ tray ← tract（拉，同 attract 吸引）→ 描画出来
posthumous§The posthumous edition includes four chapters the author had cut, and the book is worse for it.§这个**身后出版的**版本收入了作者删掉的四章，这本书因此变差了。§post（在后）+ hum（土，同 humus 腐殖质）→ 入土之后
potence§The potence of the drug falls by half after nine months, and the storage instructions never say so.§这种药的**效力**九个月后减半，而储存说明从未提及。§pot（能力，同 potential 潜力）
potentate§The potentate ruled four provinces from a room that visitors described as smaller than a schoolhouse.§这位**统治者**从一间访客形容比校舍还小的屋子里统治四个省。§pot（能力，同 power 权力）
practicality§The practicality of the plan was never tested, and the pilot ran for four weeks in ideal weather.§这个方案的**可行性**从未被检验——试点在理想天气下运行了四周。§
practitioner§The practitioner who saw her first had been in the job nine weeks and made the correct diagnosis.§第一个接诊她的**从业者**入职九周，却做出了正确诊断。§practic（实践）
pragmatic§Her pragmatic solution offended everyone's principles and solved the problem in about four days.§她**务实的**方案冒犯了所有人的原则，也在约四天内解决了问题。§
pragmatism§Pragmatism won the argument and lost the funding, since the grant was written for the ambitious version.§**实用主义**赢了辩论输了经费，因为拨款是为那个雄心勃勃的版本写的。§
pragmatist§The pragmatist on the panel asked what it would cost, and nobody had prepared an answer.§评审组里那位**实用主义者**问了成本，而没人准备好答案。§
praiseworthy§The effort was praiseworthy and the outcome was not, and the report should have said both.§这份努力**值得称道**而结果不然，报告本该把两点都说出来。§praise（赞扬）+ worthy（值得）
prank§The prank cost nine hundred pounds to undo and is still described, forty years later, as worth it.§这场**恶作剧**花了九百英镑才收拾干净，四十年后仍被说成值得。§
preachy§The book turns preachy in its last four chapters, and every reviewer said so in almost the same words.§这本书在最后四章变得**说教**，每位评论者都用几乎相同的字眼指出这点。§preach（布道）
precarious§Her position was precarious for nine months and became, after one good quarter, unassailable.§她的处境**岌岌可危**了九个月，在一个好季度之后变得无懈可击。§prec（祈求，同 pray 祈祷）→ 得靠求人施舍
precede§Four warnings preceded the collapse, and each of them was filed and none of them was acted on.§坍塌**之前**有四次警告，每一次都被归档，没有一次被处理。§pre（在前）+ ced（走，同 recede 后退）
precipitate§A single missed payment precipitated a crisis that had been four years in the making.§一次漏付**促成**了一场酝酿四年的危机。§pre（在前）+ cipit ← caput（头，同 capital 首都）→ 一头栽下去
precipitous§The decline was precipitous rather than gradual: nine hundred subscribers in a single month.§这次下滑是**陡然**而非渐进的——一个月九百名订户。§
precise§The instruction was precise and wrong, which is more dangerous than being vague and right.§这条指令**精确**而错误，这比含糊而正确更危险。§pre（在前）+ cis（切，同 scissors 剪刀）→ 事先切得齐整
precision§The precision claimed is four decimal places, and the instrument is accurate to about one.§宣称的**精度**是小数点后四位，而仪器的准确度约为一位。§
preclude§Nothing in the rules precludes it, and nobody has done it in the forty years the rules have existed.§规则里没有任何内容**排除**这种做法，而规则存在的四十年里没人这么做过。§pre（在前）+ clud（关闭，同 include 包括）→ 事先关上门
precocious§The precocious student finished the degree at nineteen and took four years off before starting anything else.§这位**早慧的**学生十九岁完成学位，然后休息四年才开始做别的。§pre（提前）+ coc（煮熟，同 concoct 调制）→ 早熟
precursor§The 1911 device was a precursor of the modern one and worked on an entirely different principle.§1911 年的那件装置是现代版的**先驱**，而原理完全不同。§pre（在前）+ curs（跑，同 current 水流）
predetermine§The outcome was predetermined in a meeting four days earlier, and the vote took eleven minutes.§结果在四天前的一次会议上就已**预先决定**，而投票用了十一分钟。§pre（在前）+ determine（决定）
predictable§The failure was predictable and predicted, and the memo predicting it is dated nine months earlier.§这次失败是**可预见的**，也确实有人预见了，那份预测它的备忘录早了九个月。§
prediction§The prediction was right about the direction and wrong about the timing by about four years.§这个**预测**方向对了，时间上错了约四年。§
predictive§The model is predictive for large sites and useless for the four hundred small ones it also covers.§这个模型对大型场址**有预测力**，对它同样涵盖的四百个小型场址则毫无用处。§
predilection§His predilection for difficult cases meant his success rate looked worse than anyone else's.§他对疑难案件的**偏好**意味着他的成功率看着比谁都差。§pre（在前）+ dilect（喜爱，同 delight 愉快）
predominant§The predominant view held for forty years and rested, it turned out, on four misread samples.§这种**占主导的**观点维持了四十年，结果它建立在四份被误读的样本上。§pre（在前）+ domin（主人，同 dominate 支配）
preeminence§Her preeminence in the field was undisputed everywhere except in her own department, where it went entirely unrewarded.§她在这一领域的**卓越**地位处处无人争议，唯独在自己系里毫无回报。§pre（在前）+ eminent（杰出的）
preliminary§The preliminary figure was published, corrected four times, and quoted in its original form for nine years.§这个**初步的**数字被公布、修正四次，却以最初形态被引用了九年。§pre（在前）+ limin（门槛，同 eliminate 排除）
premature§The announcement was premature by about four months, and two competitors used the interval well.§这次宣布**过早**了约四个月，两个竞争对手把这段时间用得很好。§pre（提前）+ mature（成熟）
prepossess§His manner prepossessed the committee within four minutes, and the references never got read.§他的举止四分钟内就让委员会**心生好感**，推荐信始终没被读过。§pre（在前）+ possess（占有）→ 先占住人心
prescience§The memo's prescience is remarkable: it names four risks and the order in which they arrived.§这份备忘录的**先见之明**了不起——它点出四项风险，以及它们到来的顺序。§pre（在前）+ sci（知道，同 science 科学）
prescient§Her prescient warning about the supplier was filed under "general correspondence" and only found nine years later.§她关于那家供应商**有先见之明的**警告被归入「一般来函」，九年后才被找到。§
prescribe§The regulations prescribe four steps and forbid the shortcut that everyone in the trade actually uses.§这些规定**规定**了四个步骤，并禁止业内人人实际使用的那条捷径。§pre（在前）+ scrib（写，同 describe 描述）
prescriptive§The guidance is prescriptive about form and silent about substance, which is the wrong way round.§这份指引在形式上**规定详尽**，在实质上一言不发，而这恰好弄反了。§
prestige§The prestige of the post is high and the salary is not, which narrows the field considerably.§这个职位的**声望**很高而薪水不高，这大大缩小了候选范围。§pre（在前）+ stig（捆／魔术）
prestigious§The prestigious award has gone to nine people from the same four institutions since 1998.§这项**声望卓著的**奖自 1998 年以来颁给了同样四所机构的九个人。§
presumption§The presumption runs the other way in criminal cases, and four jurors had to be reminded of that.§刑事案件中的**推定**方向相反，有四名陪审员需要被提醒这一点。§pre（在前）+ sum（拿，同 assume 假定）
presumptive§The presumptive cause was named within a day, and the actual cause took four years to establish.§**推定的**原因一天内就被点出，而实际原因花了四年才确立。§
presumptuous§It would be presumptuous to speak for the families, and four organizations have done it anyway.§代表这些家庭发言是**冒昧的**，而四个组织还是这么做了。§
pretense§The pretense of consultation lasted four weeks, and the tender had been awarded before it began.§咨询的**假象**维持了四周，而标在它开始前就已授出。§pre（在前）+ tens（伸展，同 tension 张力）→ 事先摆出个样子
pretentious§The building is pretentious and the interior is superb, and only one of those is in the photographs.§这栋楼**装腔作势**而室内极佳，照片里只有其中一样。§
preternatural§Her preternatural memory for names made her the best receptionist the firm ever had.§她**异乎寻常的**记名字的能力，让她成了这家公司有过的最好的前台。§preter（超过）+ natural（自然的）
pretext§The safety review was a pretext, and the file shows the decision to close had been taken in March.§安全评估只是**借口**，卷宗显示关闭的决定三月就已做出。§pre（在前）+ text（编织，同 textile 纺织品）→ 事先编好的说辞
prevail§The narrower reading prevailed by four votes, and the wider one has been argued in every case since.§较窄的解读以四票**胜出**，而较宽的解读此后在每桩案子里都被援引。§pre（在前）+ val（力量，同 valid 有效的）
prevalent§The practice is prevalent and undocumented, which is why nobody can say what it actually costs.§这种做法**普遍存在**却无据可查，所以没人说得出它实际的代价。§
preventable§Nine of the eleven deaths were preventable, and the report says so in the fourth paragraph.§十一起死亡中有九起是**可预防的**，报告在第四段就这么说了。§
preventive§The preventive measure costs four pounds per household and saves about ninety over a decade.§这项**预防**措施每户花四英镑，十年约节省九十英镑。§
principal§The principal objection is not cost but precedent, and nobody in the meeting said so out loud.§**主要的**反对理由不是成本而是先例，而会上没人把这话说出口。§princip（首要，同 prince 王子）
pristine§The site is pristine only because a fence built for another reason kept everyone out for forty years.§这处遗址之所以**原封未动**，只因一道为别的理由建的围栏把所有人挡了四十年。§pristin（原初的）
privacy§Privacy here is architectural: four walls, one door, and no window facing the corridor.§这里的**隐私**是建筑意义上的——四面墙、一道门，没有朝走廊的窗。§priv（个人的，同 private 私人的）
proclaim§The council proclaimed the square a public space and then leased four fifths of it to a café.§议会**宣布**这个广场为公共空间，随后把它的五分之四租给了一家咖啡馆。§pro（向前）+ claim（喊，同 exclaim 惊呼）
procurement§The procurement rules require three bids, and the same firm has won nine contracts in four years.§**采购**规则要求三家投标，而同一家公司四年赢了九份合同。§pro（向前）+ cur（照料，同 cure 治愈）
prod§A prod from the auditor produced in four days what nine months of polite reminders had not.§审计员的一次**督促**在四天内换来了九个月礼貌提醒都没换来的东西。§
